original_source_statement_tex:
\label{theorem-standard-etale}
A ring map $A \to B$ is \'etale at a prime $\mathfrak q$ if and only if there
exists $g \in B$, $g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that $B_g$ is standard
\'etale over $A$.

final_content.statement:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

A scheme morphism is **étale** if it is flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified, equivalently smooth of relative dimension zero. A map $A\to B$ is **standard étale** if $B\simeq(A[t]/(f))_g$, with $f\in A[t]$ monic, $g\in A[t]$ and $f'(t)$ invertible in $B$. A map $A\to B$ is étale **at** $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ if $A\to B_h$ is étale for some $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$. An étale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ has étale maps and jointly surjective images.

A ring map $A \to B$ is \'etale at a prime $\mathfrak q$ if and only if there
exists $g \in B$, $g \not \in \mathfrak q$ such that $B_g$ is standard
\'etale over $A$.

**Precise scope:** The element g avoids q and **localizes B**, not A; B_g is standard étale as defined. The two local conditions are equivalent for arbitrary ring maps and primes of B.
